analysis.investment_thesis: Go Digit is a fast-growing digital insurer with a Berkshire-like float model, but it has only turned meaningfully profitable in FY2025 and commands a price (58x P/E, 6.3x P/B) far too rich for a business delivering 11.9% ROE — well below my 15% minimum threshold. A great price for a mediocre business beats a mediocre price for a great business, and this is an expensive price for an unproven one.
key_strengths: Exceptional revenue CAGR of 44.1% (INR 2,252 Cr → INR 9,716 Cr in 4 years), showing genuine market share gains in a large underpenetrated Indian insurance market.
Float-funded balance sheet (INR 23,333 Cr assets vs INR 4,632 Cr equity) with near-zero debt (D/E: 0.07) — structurally similar to early Berkshire's insurance model.
Prem Watsa/Fairfax backing lends credibility on underwriting discipline; high promoter holding at 73% aligns management with long-term outcomes.
key_risks: Underwriting discipline is unproven — operating income was negative in 4 of 5 years (-114, -283, 50, -269, +494 Cr); FY2025 profitability may not be durable.
ROE of 11.9% and ROCE of 10.8% are structurally below my 15% minimum — paying 6.3x book for sub-cost-of-capital returns is a losing proposition.
At 58x trailing P/E, any stumble in combined ratio, regulatory headwind, or macro shock eliminates the margin of safety entirely.
red_flags: Operating income volatile and negative for most of the company's public history — suggests no entrenched underwriting moat yet.
OCF (INR 1,604 Cr) vastly exceeds net income (INR 425 Cr) primarily due to float growth, not earnings quality — this can reverse if growth slows and claims catch up.
Other Income (INR 468 Cr in FY2024, INR 324 Cr in FY2025) is a large contributor to profitability, raising questions about core underwriting economics.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert first: what kills this investment? Go Digit goes public, trades at 58x earnings, and delivers ROE below its cost of equity for years while the market waits for the float to compound. That is the base case, not a tail risk. Insurance is a commodity product in India with dozens of players, and digital distribution lowers switching costs for customers — not a recipe for a durable pricing moat. The operating income record (-114, -283, +50, -269, +494 Cr) is the honest ledger of an insurer still searching for combined-ratio discipline. FY2025's +494 Cr operating profit is encouraging, but one year does not establish a pattern I can underwrite.

The float model is genuinely interesting — total assets of INR 23,333 Cr against equity of INR 4,632 Cr means the business is leveraged with policyholder money, Berkshire-style. But Berkshire's insurance float was built on decades of demonstrated underwriting profitability and then paired with Buffett's investment genius. Go Digit has neither the track record nor the investment portfolio quality visible in this data. At 58x P/E and 6.3x P/B for an 11.9% ROE business, I am paying a premium for hope, not evidence. Mr. Market is pricing in perfection; the business is delivering inconsistency. Pass.
